title: Top-down RPG
summary: Tile-based overhead world, characters with stats, inventory and equipment. Matches the layer layout already authored in data/maps/test.tmx.

layers.name: Paralax
layers.doc: Background that scrolls slower than the world. Note the spelling: the authored map has one L, and scripts/core/depth.py aliases it.

layers.name: Floor
layers.doc: The ground, and the layer passability is authored against. Opaque in the demo map, which is why the parallax layer beneath it is currently invisible. A tile here is ART: the engine reads what blocks movement from this layer's COMPANION layer (FloorCollision by default, or whatever this layer's pyoneer_passability property names), which the editor's collision mode creates on the first mask stroke.

layers.name: GroundClutter
layers.doc: Detail that sits on the floor and behind the player: rugs, cracks, grass.

layers.name: PlayerDepth
layers.doc: Tiles that interleave with the player -- the player sorts into this band, so a tile here can occlude or be occluded depending on y.

layers.name: Above1
layers.doc: Above the player, below the foreground. Empty in the demo map.

layers.name: Foreground
layers.doc: Draws over everything in the world: treetops, roof edges, awnings.

layers.name: entity
layers.doc: Where placed things live. An object's Type names a class in scripts/core/spawn.py's SPAWN_REGISTRY and resolves to a depth through OBJECT_CONVERTER in scripts/core/depth.py; a Type that is not registered makes the map RAISE at load, which is why this list is exactly the registry and not a wish list. What the object DOES is its pyoneer_behaviors property -- see docs/BEHAVIORS.md.

tables.name: actors
tables.title: Actors
tables.doc: Every character the game can instantiate: the player, NPCs, enemies. These column names are also the parameter keys a behavior declares with source="actors" -- docs/BEHAVIORS.md lists which behavior consumes which column.

fields.name: defence
fields.doc: Damage subtracted before hp is reduced.

fields.name: speed
fields.doc: Movement rate. The engine's own field is GameEntity.move_speed and its config key is move_speed (config/entity.json, default 20) -- this column is spelled differently, and the platformer pack spells it move_speed, so a movement behavior declaring a source="actors" parameter cannot satisfy both packs under one key until they agree. Renaming this column is a change to tools/check_editor.py as well; do it there, not here alone.

fields.name: playable
fields.doc: Authoring metadata only -- NOTHING reads this at runtime. What actually decides who the human drives is the player_input token in the object's pyoneer_behaviors list; see docs/BEHAVIORS.md. Kept as a designer-facing filter, not as a switch.

tables.name: items
tables.title: Items
tables.doc: Consumables and quest objects. Equipment lives in its own table because it carries stat modifiers.

fields.name: stack_size
fields.doc: How many fit in one inventory slot.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Buy price; sell price is usually half.

tables.name: equipment
tables.title: Equipment
tables.doc: Wearable and wieldable things. Each row is one piece; the stat columns are ADDITIVE modifiers applied while equipped.

fields.name: slot
fields.doc: Which equipment slot: weapon, offhand, head, body, accessory.

fields.name: speed_mod
fields.doc: Added to the wearer's speed. Negative for heavy armour.
